instantiated_cells.justification: Lobbying may not be conducted 'as a lobbyist' unless the person is licensed and authorized, and 'lobbyist' is defined as an individual paid/receiving economic consideration to lobby (subject to the 5-days-per-reporting-period threshold).
A lobbyist license 'shall expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year,' requiring renewal every 24 months.
The statute requires a lobbyist to obtain a license under § 13.63 and separately requires each principal exceeding the threshold to file a principal registration statement under § 13.64.
The license application content specified includes a social security number and signature/fee but does not require submission of a photograph.

Public officials and legislative employees are not subject to various lobbying provisions when acting in an official capacity, and agencies/officials named in a § 13.695 statement are excluded from multiple requirements.
Agencies filing under § 13.695 and officials named are not subject to several lobbying provisions, reflecting partial exemption/relief from rules applying to non-governmental principals/lobbyists.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled sections contain no general requirement for lobbyists to notify the commission of changes in their license/registration information; only agency statements under § 13.695(2) have a 10-day change notice, which is not lobbyist registration.

No section in the bundled text sets a 'within X days after first lobbying' deadline for a lobbyist to obtain a license; § 13.66 requires licensure/authorization before lobbying, but provides no numeric day window.
